title: Segregated scheduling, reservation pools, and adaptive noise-throttling for tenant QoS
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated capacity report unpredictable throughput and occasional tail-latency spikes attributable to multi-tenant contention and unbounded burst traffic from noisy jobs. Current slab allocation and soft quotas reduce noise but do not provide per-tenant throughput guarantees or graceful throttling when capacity is saturated.

Goal: Implement a scheduling and admission control system that provides: (1) tenant reservation pools for guaranteed baseline throughput (tokens/sec equivalent), (2) hierarchical rate-limits and burst credit accounting per tenant profile, and (3) an adaptive noise-throttling controller that detects noisy neighbors and applies backpressure or eviction policies to restore QoS without manual intervention. This should integrate with the autoscaler so that scale-up decisions consider reserved capacity and burst headroom while protecting SLOs for higher-tier tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline throughput guarantees: 95% of test tenants in reserved pools achieve >= 90% of their committed tokens/sec over a 10-minute window under mixed load in the staging cluster
Noise detection: noisy-job detector identifies heavy KV-cache churn or >3x median GPU utilization spikes and raises an alert in <30s
Noise mitigation: when noisy neighbor mitigation is exercised, affected high-tier tenants restore tail P99 latency to within 1.5x of baseline within 120s
Autoscaler integration: scale decisions include reserved capacity and report an observable 'reservation headroom' metric; no SLA regressions in canary runs
Config + rollback: feature is behind a feature flag per-cluster and can be toggled without instance restarts
Documentation: operator runbook, public FAQ for Dedicated customers, and SDK config reference published
E2E tests: synthetic multi-tenant scenarios added to the CI harness that exercise reservation pools, throttling, and autoscaler behavior
design_notes: We will use a two-tier admission control: a ReservationAllocator that holds soft reservations (weighted shares) and a BurstCreditLedger for transient capacity. Reservations map to tenant profiles (e.g., platinum/gold/silver) and optionally to customer-specific committed units. The noise detector combines metrics: per-tenant GPU utilization variance, KV cache eviction rate, and request queue growth. When thresholds hit, we apply a graduated policy: initial polite-request-throttle (reduce new request admission), then batch preemption of best-effort jobs, then evict long-running low-priority jobs. Trade-offs: hard reservations can lead to unused capacity; we prefer weighted reservations with configurable borrow windows. We'll expose fine-grained controls to platform operators (reservation scaling, eviction thresholds).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement ReservationAllocator and BurstCreditLedger in the scheduler service; add metadata plumbing for tenant_profile on requests. Phase 2 (3 weeks): noise detector prototype using Prometheus alerts + local aggregator; implement polite-request-throttle. Phase 3 (2 weeks): integrate with existing autoscaler to surface reservation headroom and to prefer scale-up when reserved headroom is low. Phase 4 (2 weeks): implement eviction controller and graceful preemption for best-effort jobs; add feature-flag and operator API. Phase 5 (1 week): CI tests, canary rollout, runbooks and docs.
rollout_plan: Start with internal canary on staging-dedicated cluster with simulated tenants. Enable for non-production customers in a single region behind feature flag. Run 2 weeks of traffic replay experiments and SLO verification. Expand to 10 small production tenants with opt-in. If metrics stable, flip default for new Dedicated tenants and offer migration guidance for existing customers. Full cluster flip only after 90-day canary and ops sign-off. Rollback path: toggle feature flag to revert to previous scheduler; eviction controller will mark preempted jobs as retryable.
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger accounting and reservation reconciliation. Integration tests: multi-tenant stress harness that injects noisy jobs (high KV cache churn, GPU hogging) and asserts protections. Chaos test: simulate partial node failures during active preemption. Performance test: measure scheduler overhead under 5000 TPS admission checks. Add dashboards verifying headroom, eviction rate, detected noisy tenants, and per-tenant P99 latency.
